instruction: Please implement an online trading website for bidding and trading. The website should have functionalities for bidding and trading, allowing users to browse trading opportunities, place orders, manage their trading accounts, and view their trading history. Set the background color to lemon chiffon and the component color to chocolate.

ui_instruct.task: Navigate to the bidding section and place a bid on a trading opportunity.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The bid is successfully placed and reflected in the user's bid history, with all relevant details accurately recorded.

ui_instruct.task: Browse the available trading opportunities on the website.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A comprehensive list of trading opportunities is displayed, relevant to the user's preferences, without any missing or irrelevant entries.

ui_instruct.task: View the user's trading history from the account dashboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A detailed and accurate history of all past trading and bidding activities is displayed, including dates and transaction details.

ui_instruct.task: Update account information via the account management page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The information is updated successfully, and a confirmation message is displayed, with changes reflected correctly on subsequent views.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'lemon chiffon' as the background color and 'chocolate' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'lemon chiffon' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'chocolate', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The browse page is getting crowded — build me a proper screener for the catalog. Start me off with exactly these seven listings, I'll grow it later: 1968 Rolex Submariner (Collectibles, current bid $4,200.00, +5.25% this session, 12 bids, seller Harbor Trade Co, Open, closes July 21), 10oz Silver Bullion Bar (Metals, $310.00, -1.10%, 4 bids, MetalWorks, Open, closes July 18), Signed First-Edition Dune (Collectibles, $850.00, +5.25%, 7 bids, PageTurners, Open, closes July 25), Antique Oak Writing Desk (Furniture, $1,150.00, -0.40%, 9 bids, Harbor Trade Co, Closing, closes July 17), Gold Krugerrand Coin (Metals, $2,050.00, +2.75%, 15 bids, MetalWorks, Open, closes July 30), Persian Heriz Rug (Furniture, $980.00, -3.60%, 2 bids, Attic Finds, Open, closes July 22), and 1974 Fender Stratocaster (Collectibles, $3,300.00, +6.40%, 21 bids, Attic Finds, already Settled). I want category checkboxes where ticking two means show either one, typed min and max price boxes and a status picker that all narrow together, a live match counter that always agrees with what's actually on screen, and a way to save a filter combo under a name and load it back later. Two things I care about everywhere in this app, now and for anything we add later: session changes always display signed with two decimals like +5.25% or -1.10%, and a listing's status always shows as a colored pill — green for Open, amber for Closing, gray for Settled.

ui_instruct.task: On the screener, check the Collectibles and Metals category boxes, type 800 into the minimum price field, and set the status filter to Open.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly three listings show: 1968 Rolex Submariner, Signed First-Edition Dune, and Gold Krugerrand Coin — the 1974 Fender Stratocaster stays hidden even though it's a Collectible over $800, because it's Settled.

ui_instruct.task: Check only the Metals category box on the screener, then additionally check the Furniture box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: With Metals alone the live match counter reads 2 with exactly the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar and Gold Krugerrand Coin visible; after adding Furniture the counter reads 4 and both furniture listings join the results — categories combine as either-or, not both-and.

ui_instruct.task: With only the Metals box checked, save the search as a preset named 'Metals watch', clear all filters, then load the 'Metals watch' preset.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Clearing filters brings back all 7 listings; loading the preset re-applies the Metals filter and the results return to exactly the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar and Gold Krugerrand Coin.

ui_instruct.task: Filter the screener to the Metals category, open the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar listing, place a bid of 360, then open the trading history.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The 360 bid on the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar appears as a new entry in the trading history.

ui_instruct.task: Open the trading history section of the account area.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A trading history view renders without errors, showing past trading and bidding activity (or a sensible empty state if nothing has happened yet).

follow_ups.source_feature: Auction countdown timer per listing (reshaped into close-state-aware final-bid mechanics)
follow_ups.instruction: Bidding feels like a black box — give every listing a proper bid ticket. As I type an amount it should live-calculate the 12.5% buyer's premium, the flat $25.00 handling fee, and the total due, rounded to the cent with half-cents rounding up. Enforce increments too: a bid has to top the current bid by at least $50 while the current bid is under $1,000, and by at least $100 once it's $1,000 or more — and tell me the exact floor when I'm short. One more habit I want everywhere in this app from now on, for anything that commits money or can't be undone: show me a summary to confirm before it goes through, starting with this ticket, whose confirmed bids land in my trading history like always. And Settled listings shouldn't accept bids at all.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bid ticket on the Signed First-Edition Dune listing and type 905 as your bid amount.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Before any submit, the ticket live-shows a buyer's premium of $113.13, a $25.00 handling fee, and a total due of $1,043.13 — the half-cent on the premium rounds up, so $113.13 rather than $113.12.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bid ticket on the Gold Krugerrand Coin, type 2100, then change it to 2150.
ui_instruct.expected_result: 2100 is rejected with a message about the $100 minimum increment (current bid is $2,050.00 so the floor is $2,150.00) and cannot be submitted; changing to 2150 clears the error and the ticket becomes submittable.

ui_instruct.task: On the Signed First-Edition Dune bid ticket, type 900, then delete the amount so the field is empty.
ui_instruct.expected_result: While 900 is typed the total due reads $1,037.50 without submitting anything; once the field is emptied the ticket falls back to a calm neutral state — no NaN, no crash, no stale total left behind.

ui_instruct.task: Bid 360 on the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar through the ticket, go through the confirmation step, then open the trading history.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A confirmation summary appears first showing the $360.00 bid and the $430.00 total due; after confirming, the bid shows up in the trading history.

ui_instruct.task: On the screener, check the Collectibles and Metals category boxes, type 800 into the minimum price field, and set the status filter to Open.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly three listings show: 1968 Rolex Submariner, Signed First-Edition Dune, and Gold Krugerrand Coin — the 1974 Fender Stratocaster stays hidden even though it's a Collectible over $800, because it's Settled.

follow_ups.instruction: I keep losing track of the lots I care about — add starring. Let me star or unstar from the browse listings and from the screener results, with a My Watchlist section on the dashboard showing everything I've starred plus a summary strip with the combined current-bid value and each item's status pill. Pre-star the Gold Krugerrand Coin and the Antique Oak Writing Desk for me. Also drop a watched-only toggle into that screener you built, stacking on top of whatever other filters are already on. And if I unstar everything, the watchlist should say so nicely rather than going blank.

ui_instruct.task: Open the My Watchlist section on the dashboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Gold Krugerrand Coin and Antique Oak Writing Desk are there from the start, the combined current-bid value reads $3,200.00, and the Desk wears the amber Closing pill.

ui_instruct.task: From the browse listings, star the Persian Heriz Rug, then open My Watchlist.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The watchlist now holds 3 items and the combined current-bid value reads $4,180.00 — updated immediately, no reload needed.

ui_instruct.task: In My Watchlist, unstar the Gold Krugerrand Coin and the Antique Oak Writing Desk.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The watchlist empties gracefully into a friendly empty-state message — no blank screen, no $NaN or leftover stale total.

ui_instruct.task: On the screener, turn on the watched-only toggle and check the Metals category box, then turn the watched-only toggle back off.
ui_instruct.expected_result: With both on, only the Gold Krugerrand Coin matches (watched AND Metals together); toggling watched-only off brings the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar back alongside it.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bid ticket on the Signed First-Edition Dune listing and type 905 as your bid amount.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Before any submit, the ticket live-shows a buyer's premium of $113.13, a $25.00 handling fee, and a total due of $1,043.13 — the half-cent on the premium rounds up, so $113.13 rather than $113.12.

follow_ups.source_feature: Price results / past sales lookup (extended into the settlement workflow that produces the results)
follow_ups.instruction: Time to actually close auctions. Any listing in Closing status gets a close-and-settle flow: first an invoice review showing the winning bid with the same 12.5% buyer's premium and $25.00 handling the bid ticket charges, then it commits and the listing flips to Settled everywhere it appears. Every settlement lands on a new Completed Sales page as a record with the item, seller, hammer price and fee-inclusive total, searchable by item or seller name. Seed it with the Fender sale that already happened — hammer $3,300.00 by Attic Finds, total $3,737.50. Open listings shouldn't offer settling, only Closing ones.

ui_instruct.task: Start the close-and-settle flow on the Antique Oak Writing Desk and look at the invoice review step.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The invoice shows the winning bid of $1,150.00, a buyer's premium of $143.75, a $25.00 handling fee, and a total due of $1,318.75.

ui_instruct.task: Settle the Antique Oak Writing Desk all the way through its confirmation, then find the Desk on the browse listings.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Desk now wears the gray Settled pill on browse and no longer offers bidding; it also stops matching the screener's Closing status filter.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Completed Sales page, type 'Attic' into its search box, then replace it with 'zzz'.
ui_instruct.expected_result: On first load the seeded 1974 Fender Stratocaster sale is listed with a $3,737.50 total; searching 'Attic' narrows to that Attic Finds sale; 'zzz' shows a friendly no-results state instead of a blank or broken page.

ui_instruct.task: Bid 1250 on the Antique Oak Writing Desk through the bid ticket and confirm it, then start the close-and-settle flow on the Desk.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The invoice picks up the fresh $1,250.00 winning bid and the total due reads $1,431.25 — the same premium-plus-handling math the bid ticket previews.

ui_instruct.task: Check only the Metals category box on the screener, then additionally check the Furniture box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: With Metals alone the live match counter reads 2 with exactly the 10oz Silver Bullion Bar and Gold Krugerrand Coin visible; after adding Furniture the counter reads 4 and both furniture listings join the results — categories combine as either-or, not both-and.

follow_ups.instruction: Give my dashboard a Market Movers panel: three columns — Top Gainers and Top Losers by session change, and Most Active by bid count — top three in each. Only count listings still in play; anything Settled sits out no matter how big its move or how many bids it collected. If two listings tie on change percent, the one with the higher current bid goes first. And bids I place through the ticket should feed the Most Active counts right away.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Market Movers panel on the dashboard and read the Top Gainers column.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Top Gainers reads 1968 Rolex Submariner, Signed First-Edition Dune, Gold Krugerrand Coin in that order — the 1974 Fender Stratocaster (+6.40%) is absent because it's Settled, and the Rolex outranks the Dune on their +5.25% tie because its current bid is higher.

ui_instruct.task: Read the Top Losers column of the Market Movers panel.
ui_instruct.expected_result: It lists Persian Heriz Rug, 10oz Silver Bullion Bar, Antique Oak Writing Desk in that order, with their changes shown as -3.60%, -1.10% and -0.40%.

ui_instruct.task: Read the Most Active column of the Market Movers panel.
ui_instruct.expected_result: It lists Gold Krugerrand Coin (15 bids), 1968 Rolex Submariner (12), Antique Oak Writing Desk (9) — the Fender's 21 bids don't count since it's Settled.

ui_instruct.task: Bid 1250 on the Antique Oak Writing Desk through the bid ticket, confirm it, then return to the Market Movers panel.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Desk's entry in Most Active now shows 10 bids while the order stays Krugerrand, Rolex, Desk.

ui_instruct.task: Open the bid ticket on the Gold Krugerrand Coin, type 2100, then change it to 2150.
ui_instruct.expected_result: 2100 is rejected with a message about the $100 minimum increment (current bid is $2,050.00 so the floor is $2,150.00) and cannot be submitted; changing to 2150 clears the error and the ticket becomes submittable.

follow_ups.instruction: I want price context before I bid — give each listing a detail view with a session-close price chart. For the Rolex, its last eight session closes were 3900, 4050, 3980, 4120, 4060, 4150, 4180, 4200, oldest to newest; make up sensible histories for the rest. I need a line/bar toggle, 1W and 1M timeframe buttons (last five sessions versus all eight) with a high/low readout that recomputes for whatever window is showing, and a little price-level box — as I type a number it draws a line at that level and tells me how many of the visible sessions closed above it, updating with every keystroke.

ui_instruct.task: Open the 1968 Rolex Submariner detail view and switch the chart to the 1W timeframe.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The window readout shows a low of $4,060.00 and a high of $4,200.00 — not the all-time low of $3,900.00, which only belongs to the 1M view.

ui_instruct.task: On the Rolex chart with 1M selected, type 4100 into the price-level input, then replace it with 50.
ui_instruct.expected_result: At 4100 the readout says 4 of 8 sessions closed above the line; at 50 it says 8 of 8 — both updating live as you type, with the reference line moving on the chart.

ui_instruct.task: Switch the Rolex chart from line to bar mode, then change the timeframe to 1W while in bar mode.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The chart renders in bar mode without going blank, and after the timeframe change it stays in bar mode showing just the five-session window.

ui_instruct.task: Look at the session change figure and the status shown on the 1968 Rolex Submariner detail view.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The change reads exactly +5.25% — signed, two decimals — and the listing carries its green Open pill, matching how these appear everywhere else in the app.

ui_instruct.task: Start the close-and-settle flow on the Antique Oak Writing Desk and look at the invoice review step.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The invoice shows the winning bid of $1,150.00, a buyer's premium of $143.75, a $25.00 handling fee, and a total due of $1,318.75.

follow_ups.instruction: Let's build some trust: seller profile pages showing an average star rating (one decimal, round half-up) and all their written reviews, plus a Top Sellers leaderboard ranked by that average — ties broken by whoever has more reviews. Reviews can only be left on records in Completed Sales; listings still open for bidding get no review option anywhere. Backfill some history for me: PageTurners has three past sales reviewed at 5, 5 and 4 stars; MetalWorks two at 5 and 4; Harbor Trade Co a Georgian Side Table reviewed at 3 stars plus a Regency Mantel Clock sale at a $640.00 hammer that nobody has reviewed yet; and the Fender sale carries a 4-star review. All those backfilled sales should sit in Completed Sales too.

ui_instruct.task: Open the PageTurners seller profile.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The average rating reads 4.7 from 3 reviews — 5, 5 and 4 average to 4.666..., which rounds half-up to 4.7, not a truncated 4.6.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Top Sellers leaderboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The order reads PageTurners 4.7, MetalWorks 4.5, Attic Finds 4.0, Harbor Trade Co 3.0.

ui_instruct.task: From the Completed Sales page, leave a 5-star review on Harbor Trade Co's Regency Mantel Clock sale, then check the Top Sellers leaderboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Harbor Trade Co's average becomes 4.0 (3 and 5 stars) and it now sits above Attic Finds — the two are tied at 4.0 and Harbor wins the tie with 2 reviews to Attic's 1.

ui_instruct.task: Settle the Antique Oak Writing Desk through its confirmation, then open the Completed Sales page and find the Desk's new record.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The freshly settled Desk sale appears in Completed Sales and offers a review option right there — while listings still open for bidding offer no way to leave a review.

ui_instruct.task: Open the My Watchlist section on the dashboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Gold Krugerrand Coin and Antique Oak Writing Desk are there from the start, the combined current-bid value reads $3,200.00, and the Desk wears the amber Closing pill.

follow_ups.instruction: Now a calendar page: a July 2026 month grid with each still-active listing sitting on its close date — the dates I gave you when we set up the screener. Settled lots stay off it entirely. Give me category chips and a watched-only toggle that narrow together rather than replacing each other, let me click an entry to jump to that listing, and days with no closings should just sit as quiet empty cells.

ui_instruct.task: Open the auction calendar.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The July 2026 grid shows entries on exactly the 17th (Antique Oak Writing Desk), 18th (10oz Silver Bullion Bar), 21st (1968 Rolex Submariner), 22nd (Persian Heriz Rug), 25th (Signed First-Edition Dune) and 30th (Gold Krugerrand Coin) — six in all, with nothing for the settled Fender.

ui_instruct.task: On the calendar, turn on the watched-only toggle, then also select the Metals category chip.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Watched-only alone leaves just the 17th (Oak Desk) and the 30th (Krugerrand); adding Metals narrows it to the Krugerrand on the 30th only — the filters stack, they don't replace each other.

ui_instruct.task: Click the calendar entry on July 25th, then go back and look at July 19th and 20th.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The entry takes you to the Signed First-Edition Dune's listing; the 19th and 20th render as normal empty day cells — no errors, no missing grid squares.

ui_instruct.task: Star the Persian Heriz Rug from the browse listings, then open the calendar with the watched-only toggle on.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The rug's July 22nd entry now shows up alongside the 17th and the 30th — the calendar tracks the watchlist stars live.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Market Movers panel on the dashboard and read the Top Gainers column.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Top Gainers reads 1968 Rolex Submariner, Signed First-Edition Dune, Gold Krugerrand Coin in that order — the 1974 Fender Stratocaster (+6.40%) is absent because it's Settled, and the Rolex outranks the Dune on their +5.25% tie because its current bid is higher.

follow_ups.source_feature: Platform-wide consistent UI theming (extrapolated from its unified charting interface)
follow_ups.instruction: The lemon-chiffon look has run its course — sharpen the whole thing up, same pages, new skin. Every primary action button (place bid, save preset, settle, leave review) goes dark chocolate with white text in a fully-rounded pill shape; every page's main heading gets a chocolate accent bar underneath it; listing and sale cards get 12px rounded corners with a thin chocolate border; all money values switch to a monospace font; and the status pills go uppercase while keeping their colors. Apply it everywhere — browse and the screener, the dashboard with the movers panel and watchlist, Completed Sales, seller profiles, and the calendar — I don't want to stumble onto one page still wearing the old look.

ui_instruct.task: Look at the primary action buttons on the browse/screener page, such as the bid and save-preset buttons.
ui_instruct.expected_result: They're dark chocolate with white text in fully-rounded pill shapes, and every price on the page renders in a monospace font.

ui_instruct.task: Open the dashboard and inspect the Market Movers panel, the My Watchlist cards, and the page heading.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Cards have 12px rounded corners with a thin chocolate border, the main heading carries the chocolate accent bar underneath, and status pills read in uppercase while keeping their green/amber/gray colors.

ui_instruct.task: Visit the Completed Sales page, any seller profile, and the auction calendar, checking money values and headings on each.
ui_instruct.expected_result: All three pages show monospace money values and the accent-bar heading — and on Completed Sales the 1974 Fender Stratocaster total still reads exactly $3,737.50.

ui_instruct.task: Find the Antique Oak Writing Desk's entry on the auction calendar and check its status pill.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Despite the restyle it still wears the amber Closing pill (now in uppercase), keeping the app-wide green/amber/gray status coding.

ui_instruct.task: Open the PageTurners seller profile.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The average rating reads 4.7 from 3 reviews — 5, 5 and 4 average to 4.666..., which rounds half-up to 4.7, not a truncated 4.6.

target_app_summary: The little lemon-chiffon bidding site has grown into a full auction-trading platform. Discovery got serious: a multi-criteria screener with saved presets over a pinned seven-lot catalog, a starred watchlist with live value rollups, a Market Movers panel with tie-aware rankings, and a July 2026 close-date calendar that cross-filters by category and watchlist. Trading mechanics deepened: a live bid ticket computes tiered increments and fee-inclusive totals per keystroke, and a close-and-settle workflow turns Closing lots into searchable Completed Sales records using the same fee schedule. Community and context layers sit on top — seller profiles with half-up-rounded ratings and a tie-broken leaderboard gated on settled sales, and per-listing price-history charts with windowed high/low stats — before a final chocolate-pill restyle sweeps every surface. The feature graph runs one deep chain (bid ticket -> settlement -> reputation) alongside a discovery cluster (screener -> watchlist -> calendar) and movers fed by ticket activity.

edges.what: extends base bid placement and trading history
watched-only toggle composes with screener filters
invoice applies the ticket's fee schedule and latest high bid
ticket bids update counts feeding Most Active ranking
adds detail chart onto base catalog listings
reviews gated on Completed Sales records from settlement
watched-only calendar filter driven by watchlist stars
restyles base browse and history pages

global_rules.rule: Session change percentages always display signed with exactly two decimals (e.g. +5.25%, -1.10%) on every surface.
Listing status always renders as a colored pill badge — green Open, amber Closing, gray Settled — wherever a listing appears.
Any money-committing or irreversible action (bids, settlements) always shows a confirmation summary before executing.
